faqs.question: What does PRA Identification Test (Class I) measure?
faqs.answer: The PRA Identification Test measures the presence of antibodies in a recipient's blood against specific human leukocyte antigens (HLA) Class I.

faqs.question: Why is PRA Identification Test (Class I) done?
faqs.answer: • To assess compatibility between a transplant recipient and a potential donor • To reduce the risk of rejection after organ transplantation • To guide treatment decisions for individuals requiring organ transplants • To evaluate the effectiveness of immunosuppressive therapy

faqs.question: When is PRA Identification Test (Class I) recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended for individuals who • are candidates for organ transplantation, such as kidney or liver transplant, • have had previous organ transplants and require ongoing monitoring, • require adjustments to immunosuppressive medication, or • are involved in living donor programs to ensure compatibility.

faqs.question: What if the results of the PRA Identification Test (Class I) are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate a higher risk of organ rejection or a lower chance of finding a compatible donor.

faqs.question: What to expect during the PRA Identification Test (Class I)?
faqs.answer: A blood sample will be collected from your arm. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the PRA Identification Test (Class I)?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications or supplements you are taking. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any additional instructions provided by your healthcare provider regarding discontinuation of immunosuppressive medication before the test.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with PRA Identification Test?
faqs.answer: Crossmatching: This test determines if a potential donor's organ is compatible with the recipient's immune system. HLA Typing: It identifies the specific HLA antigens present in an individual's blood to assess compatibility for transplantation.

faqs.question: What is the PRA Identification Test (Class I) also known as?
What is organ transplant rejection?
faqs.answer: Organ transplant rejection occurs when the recipient's immune system recognises the transplanted organ as foreign and attacks it. Rejection can lead to organ failure.
